title: Make a new ledger entry type stop the build

blocks.text: The core banking team owns three kinds of ledger entry, `Deposit`, `Withdrawal` and `Fee`, and adds one every year or two. Reports on them are added every month by other teams in the same codebase. The last time a kind was added, the balance report learned about it and the monthly statement didn't: customers got statements that skipped the new lines, and nobody noticed for three weeks. `Reversal` is coming next.

In `src/main/java/practice/Ledger.java`, finish `balanceCents(...)` and `statementLine(...)` (the formats are in their comments), and set up `Entry` so that adding a fourth kind can't build until every method that looks at an entry's kind has been told about it. About twelve lines in total.

cases.says: the balance adds deposits and subtracts withdrawals and fees, and is zero for no entries
the statement prints each kind of entry with its sign, amount and, for a fee, its reason
Entry is sealed and permits exactly Deposit, Withdrawal and Fee, so a switch over it is checked for every kind

origin.section: When the Types Are Fixed and the Operations Grow, Seal the Hierarchy and Let javac List the Switches

concepts: Over a sealed type, adding a permitted type makes javac report every switch without a default, and a new operation is one new method; the choice between sealed and open follows who adds types.
